rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual adjective modifies the two gardens; alternatively, it predicates an omitted subject, ‘they are intensely green.’
rows.anchor: صفة لجنتان وسط بينها الأعتراض لما تقدم من التنبيه على أن تكذيب كل من الموصوف والصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interruption between the gardens and their description underscores that denying either the described thing or its attribute merits censure.
rows.anchor: التنبيه على أن تكذيب كل من الموصوف والصفة حيقي بالإنكار والتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duhma originally denotes the blackness of night and can describe a black horse; by proximity of color it can also denote fully saturated green.
rows.anchor: من الدهمة وهي في الأصل على ما قال الراغب سواد الليل ويعبر بها عن سواد الفرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form ادهام can mean becoming black or becoming intensely green; these gardens are very deep green, shading toward black.
rows.anchor: على وزن مفعال إذا اسود أو اشتدت خضرته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وعكرمة وعطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: These authorities and others explain مدهامتان as intensely green; a report from Abu Ayyub says the Prophet answered that the gardens are green.
rows.anchor: وفسرها هنا ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وعكرمة وعطاء بن أبي رباح وجماعة بخضراوان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أبي أيوب
rows.claim: Asked by Abu Ayyub about مدهامتان, the Prophet replied that the two gardens are green, meaning intensely green.
rows.anchor: سألت النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير وأبو صالح
rows.claim: They explain the dark cast of the intense green as resulting from the gardens being well watered.
rows.anchor: من الري من الماء كما روي عن ابن عباس وابن الزبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description suggests these gardens are dominated by ground-covering plants and blossoms, while the earlier gardens’ many branches suggests trees dominate there.
rows.anchor: الغالب عليهما النبات والرياحين المنبسطة على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that contrast, the present pair rank below the earlier pair, since gardens rich in shade and fruit exceed gardens with less shade and fruit.
rows.anchor: في المنزلة والقدر كيف لاوالجنة الكثيرة الظلال والثمار أعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those preferring the present gardens argue that greenery is especially praised in gardens and signals abundant water, care, and protection from withering.
rows.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى تفضيل هاتين الجنتين مع اختصاص الوصف بالخضرة بالنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is the one you kindle and draw out from the fire-sticks.
rows.anchor: أي تقدحونها وتستخرجونها من الزناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resumed sentence specifies the fire’s benefits: it reminds people of Hell because God made livelihood depend on fire, inviting them to remember its punishment.
rows.anchor: جعلناها تذكيرا لنار جهنم حيث علقنا بها أسباب المعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes earthly fire as a model of Hellfire, which is seventy times hotter according to the report in the two Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: ناركم هذه توقدون جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says, in a report found in the two Sahih collections, that the fire people kindle is one part of seventy parts of Hellfire.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ناركم هذه توقدون جزء من سبعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either account, تذكرة means remembrance opposite to forgetting; the first account does not address whether earthly fire is of Hell’s kind, while the second does.
rows.anchor: وعلى الوجهين التذكرة من الذكر المقابل للنسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the fire a proof of resurrection: bringing fire from green wood shows God can restore dispersed matter.
rows.anchor: من أخرج من النار من الشجر الأخضر المضاد لها قادر على إعادة ما تفرقت مواده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed sense illumination in darkness is rejected because تذكرة cannot mean visual perception derived from sight.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن التذكرة لا تكون بمعنى التبصرة المأخوذة من البصر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Many authorities, including Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada, transmit the explanation that the fire reminds people of Hell.
rows.anchor: وكون المراد تذكرة لنار جهنم هو المأثور عن الكثيرين ومنهم ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متاع means benefit or useful provision for those in need of fire.
rows.anchor: للذين ينزلون القواء وهي الفقر من أقوى دخل كأصحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The المقوون are people who enter barren land; القواء denotes desolation or poverty, as أقوى parallels أصحر, entered the desert.
rows.anchor: للذين ينزلون القواء وهي الفقر من أقوى دخل كأصحر دخل الصحراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barren-land dwellers are singled out because they need fire most; residents or nearby travelers are not compelled to kindle it with fire-sticks.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص المقوين بذلك لأنهم أحوج إليها فإن المقيمين أو النازلين بقرب منهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Another explanation takes المقوين as travelers; reports from Ibn Abbas, Hasan, and Qatada describe travelers running out of supplies and using fire to warm themselves.
rows.anchor: عبد بن حميد عن الحسن وهو وابن جرير وعبد الرزاق عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travelers are called المقوين because they often cross barren lands and deserts.
rows.anchor: وكان إطلاق المقوين على المسافرين لأنهم كثيرا ما يسلكون الفقراء والمفاوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view identifies the المقوين as poor people, who use fire for light and warmth; أقوى is explained as becoming poor.
rows.anchor: يستضيئون بها في الظلمة ويصطلحون من البرد كأنه تصور من حال الحاصل

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says المقوون are the hungry, with empty stomachs and provisions, who need fire to cook their food.
rows.anchor: لأنهم أقوت أي خلت بطونهم ومزاودهم من الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hungry-only explanation is remote because their needs and relief are not limited to foods that require cooking.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه بعيد لعدم انحصار ما يهمهم ويسد خلتهم

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid say the fire benefits all people, travelers and residents, by providing light, warmth, cooking, and baking.
rows.anchor: الموقين المستمتعين بها من الناس أجمعين المسافرين والحاضرين

rows.speaker: الطيبي والطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi and al-Tabarsi explain المقوي as a word of opposites: poor for lacking wealth and rich for having power over what one wants.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا القول المقوى من الأضداد يقال للفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi questions the opposites account and finds it more plausible that المقوي means one in need, since all who enjoy fire need it.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأقرب عليه أنه أريد بالأقواء الأحتياج والمستمتع محتاج إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire’s worldly benefit is mentioned last to draw attention to the more important, otherworldly benefit.
rows.anchor: لتنبيه على الأهم هو النفع الأخروي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water precedes fire because it is more urgently and widely needed and more generally useful.
rows.anchor: الاحتياج إليه أشد وأكثر والانتفاع به أعم وأوفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative order goes from creating humans to food, water for kneading it, then fire for baking it; al-Alusi calls this rationale unconvincing.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعده ما به قوام الإنسان من فائدة الحرث وهو الطعام

rows.speaker: حجر المروزي عن علي
rows.claim: Hujr al-Marwazi heard Ali recite the prior rhetorical questions about procreation, crops, water, and fire, replying ‘Rather, You, Lord’ three times after each.
rows.anchor: حجر المروي قال : بت عند علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree over whether it is recommended to answer each rhetorical question in ritual prayer with ‘Rather, You, Lord.’
rows.anchor: استحسان قول مثل ذلك في الصلاة اختلافا بين العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم may be governed by the constituent attached to the preceding lām or by مهيمن.
rows.anchor: منصوب بما تعلق به اللام من الأستقرار أو بمهيمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an omitted remember governs يوم, magnifying and making the Day awe-inspiring.
rows.anchor: بإضمار اذكر أي اذكر ذلك اليوم تعظيما له وتهويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse supplies an omitted يكون as an answer to when their punishment is: it will be on the Day He raises them.
rows.anchor: جواب لمنسألأ متى عذاب هؤلاء فقيل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making يوم governed by الكافرين is judged baseless.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بالكافرين وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جميعا may emphasize that not one of them will escape resurrection.
rows.anchor: حال جيء به للتأكيد والمعنى يبعثهم الله تعالى كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, جميعا means they will be gathered together on one plain.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون حالا غير مؤكدة أي يبعثهم مجتمعين في صعيد واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will inform them of their vile deeds by explaining that the deeds issued from them.
rows.anchor: ببيان صدورها عنهم أو بتصويرها في تلك النشأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their deeds appear in forms suited to that realm, terrifying them before witnesses and increasing their shame and punishment.
rows.anchor: الصور الهائلة على رءوس الأشهاد تخجيلا لهم وتشهيرا بحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence answers how God can report passing deeds: He counted them exhaustively, and none escaped His count.
rows.anchor: استئناف وقع جوابا عما نشأ مما قبله من السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ونسوه can be a circumstantial clause describing the deeds when God counted them, with or without an implicit قد.
rows.anchor: حال منمفعول أحصى بإضمار قد أو بدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they forgot their deeds, so God will disclose them and show that the punishment they witness came from those deeds, deepening reproach and regret.
rows.anchor: أحصاه الله تعالى ونسوهفينبئهم به ليعرفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing at all is absent from God’s witness; this parenthetical conclusion confirms His exhaustive recording of their deeds.
rows.anchor: لا يغيب عنه أمر من الأمور أصلا والجملة اعتراض تذييلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse is cited as evidence that God’s witness encompasses all things in the heavens and earth, whether contained in or constitutive of them.
rows.anchor: استشهاد على شمول شهادته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators take the clause as coordinated with the emigrants; it refers to the Helpers (Ansar).
rows.anchor: الأكثرون على أنه معطوف على المهاجرين والمراد بهم الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabawwu means settling in a place; al-mabāʾa is a dwelling place.
rows.anchor: والتبوؤ النزول في المكان ومنه المباءة للمنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abode is Medina, and defining it as the abode honors it as the true abode God prepared for the Helpers.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها المدينة ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred construction metaphorically makes faith a settled homeland, using an implicit metaphor and its figurative completion.
rows.anchor: فباعتبار جعله مستقرا ومتوطنا على سبيل الاستعارة المكنية التخييلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another construction uses a poetic pattern: they settled in the abode and made faith sincere.
rows.anchor: علفتها تبنا وماءا باردا + أيتبوأو الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation treats settling as a metonym for its necessary consequence, staying in the abode and faith.
rows.anchor: التبوؤ مجاز مرسل عن اللزوم وهو لازم معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing supplies abode before faith, yielding the abode of migration and the abode of faith; al-Alusi finds this strained.
rows.anchor: حذف مضاف أي ودار الإيمان فكأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggestion that الإيمان itself metaphorically means Medina, as the place where faith appears, is dismissed.
rows.anchor: إن الإيمان مجاز عن المدينة سمي محل ظهور الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the conjunction to mean together with their faith is also rejected.
rows.anchor: الواو للمعية والمراد تبوأوا الدار مع إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Dār is a conventional name for Medina, alongside al-Madīna, Ṭayba, Ṭāba, Yathrib, and Jābira.
rows.anchor: علم بالغلبة على المدينة كالمدينة وأنه أحد أسماء لها منها طيبة وطابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before them means before the emigrants and attaches to تبوؤوا, with an implicit reference to their migration.
rows.anchor: أي من قبل المهاجرين والجار متعلق بتبوأوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This wording need not claim that the Helpers believed before the emigrants, only that their faith was already firmly established and undisputed.
rows.anchor: ولا يلزم منه سبق إيمانهم ليقال : إن الأمر بالعكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A permissible refinement is that the Helpers preceded the emigrants in being settled in faith, since they did not contest it when the emigrants displayed theirs.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد سبق الأنصار لهم في أصل الإيمان بل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reversed-order reading makes the Helpers precede the emigrants only in settling the abode; al-Alusi rejects it as contrary to the apparent order and lacking a subtle rationale.
rows.anchor: الكلام على التقديم والتأخير والتقدير تبوأوا الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the verse establishes only that the Helpers’ combined settlement and faith preceded the emigrants’; the author disputes that one earlier component suffices.
rows.anchor: ما تدل الآية عليه تقدممجموع تبويء الأنصاري وإيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be a circumstantial description of the Helpers or a new sentence.
rows.anchor: إليهم ( في موضع الحالمن الموصول وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation treats their love as a figure for supporting emigrants without resentment or weariness when they need help.
rows.anchor: والكلام قيل : كناية عن مواساتهم المهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Literally, they love emigrants because they migrated to them, out of love for faith.
rows.anchor: لحبهم الإيمان ( ولا يجدون في صدورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They feel no desire for any portion of the spoils or other goods given to the emigrants; their souls do not covet it.
rows.anchor: ما أعطى المهاجرون ولم تطمع إلى شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here حاجة means something one needs; وجد denotes practical awareness, and locating it in the chest is figurative.
rows.anchor: فالوجدان إدراك عملي وكونه في الصدر من باب المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من may be partitive, explanatory with an omitted noun, or causal; the deleted noun طلب explains why the need never entered their minds.
rows.anchor: تبعيضية وجوز كونها بيانية والكلام على حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes حاجة as resentment, anger, envy, or covetousness caused by the emigrants’ allotments; al-Alusi prefers the preceding explanation.
rows.anchor: ولا يجدون في صدورهم ( أي ولا يعلمون في أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of يؤثرون need not be restricted to the emigrants; the phrase may mean preferring them in everything.
rows.anchor: لا يعتبر مفعول يؤثرون خصوص المهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خصاصة is need or poverty, named from the gaps and openings left between the slats of a house.
rows.anchor: حاجة من خصاص البيت وهو ما يبقى بين عيدانهمن الفرج والفتوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ولو clause is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: والجملة في موضع الحال وقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi defines شح as meanness and a tight, avid soul inclined to withhold, citing a poetic line; it is innate, while bukhl is withholding one’s own wealth.
rows.anchor: وهو أن تكون النفس كزة حريصة على المنع

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines شح as stinginess combined with habitual greed.
rows.anchor: الشح بخل مع حرص وذلك فيما كان عادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasan distinguishes bukhl as withholding what one possesses and شح as coveting what others possess.
rows.anchor: والشح أن يشح على ما في يدي الناس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: When a man feared he was doomed because he was miserly, Ibn Masud said this was bukhl, not the verse’s شح; that شح is consuming another’s wealth unjustly.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنرجلا قال له : إني أخاف

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says merely withholding one’s own wealth is bukhl; شح is desiring what one does not own.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds no lexicographic support for those reports as formal definitions, but understands شح as extreme greed that resents others’ generosity, consumes their wealth, or covets what is not one’s own.
rows.anchor: لم أر لأحد من اللغويين شيئا من هذه التفاسير للشح

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa and Ibn Abi Abla read يُوقَ with a doubled qaf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبيعبلة ( ومن يوق ) بشد القاف

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Umar and Ibn Abi Abla read شح with kasra on the shin; the readings have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عمر وابن أبيعبلة ( شح ) بكسر الشين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being protected from the self’s greed comes through God’s enabling help, so one resists its dominant love of wealth and dislike of spending.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية ومنيوق بتوفيق الله تعالى ومعونته شحنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Helpers put emigrants before themselves in every kind of good thing, even arranging a guest’s food while their household went without.
rows.anchor: أكرمي ضيف رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a hungry visitor came to the Prophet, who sought a host; an Ansari, Abu Talha in one version, fed him while his family went without, and the Prophet said God marveled at them.
rows.anchor: يا رسول الله أصابني الجهد فأرسل إلى نسائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports a sheep’s head passed among seven Companions’ households, each preferring the next, until it returned to the first; the verse was revealed about them.
rows.anchor: تداوله أهل سبعة أبيات حتى رجع إلى الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful are those who attain every desired good and escape every harm.
rows.anchor: الفائزون بكل مطلوب الناجون من كلمكروه

words: وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional conclusion is a fitting summation and praise, primarily encompassing the Helpers; singular من followed by plural أولئك tracks form then meaning and suggests few attain it in number but great stature.
rows.anchor: والجملة الشرطية تذييل حسن ومدح للأنصار بما هو غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse strongly censures greed.
rows.anchor: ويفهم من الآية ذم الشح جدا وقد وردت أخبار كثيرة بذمه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أنس
rows.claim: A report from Anas says nothing has destroyed Islam as thoroughly as greed.
rows.anchor: عن أنس مرفوعا ما محق الإسلام محق الشح قط

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits that faith and greed never coexist in a servant’s heart, nor do the dust of God’s path and Hellfire’s smoke; the collector graded it sound.
rows.anchor: عن أبيهريرة مرفوعا لا يجتمع غبار في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أبي سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet says that stinginess and bad character do not coexist in a Muslim; al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb.
rows.anchor: عن أبيسعيد الخدري مرفوعا خصلتانلا يجتمعان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that God created Eden and its trees, which answered ‘The believers have succeeded’; God vowed that no miser would dwell there, and the Prophet recited this verse.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: The Prophet commands avoiding injustice and greed, saying greed destroyed earlier peoples by driving them to bloodshed and violating sacred limits.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله أن رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : اتقوا الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protection from greed does not require giving away everything: paying zakat, hosting guests, and meeting hardship count as freedom from greed.
rows.anchor: ينبغي أنيعلم أن تقوي الشح لا تتوقف على أن يكون الرجل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن مجمع بن يحيى
rows.claim: The Prophet says the person who pays zakat, hosts a guest, and gives in times of hardship is free of greed.
rows.anchor: عن مجمع بن يحيى مرفوعا بريء من الشح من أدى الزكاة

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله وأنس
rows.claim: Al-Alusi notes comparable reports from Jabir and Anas on being free of greed through such conduct.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله ما يقرب منه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says that whoever pays zakat on his wealth has been protected from greed.
rows.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال : من أدى زكاة ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khāliq is explained either as determining things according to wisdom or originating them without prior material or model; creation can also mean producing one thing from another.
rows.anchor: المقدر للأشياء على مقتضى الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bāriʾ brings things into existence free from discrepancy, as wisdom and their nature require; it can also mean distinguishing them by differing forms.
rows.anchor: الموجد لها بريئة من تفاوت ما تقتضيه بحسب الحكمة والجبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muṣawwir brings each thing’s form and qualities into existence as He wills.
rows.anchor: الموجد لصورها وكيفياتها كما أراد

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines image as the form by which entities are imprinted and distinguished, either sensible to common people and specialists or intellectual, apprehended only by specialists.
rows.anchor: الصورة ما تنتقش بها الأعيان وتتميز بها عن غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raghib links these two kinds of form to ‘We created you, then fashioned you’ and other verses.
rows.anchor: بقوله سبحانه : ( خلقناكم ثم صورناكم )

rows.speaker: علي وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة والحسن وابن السمقيع
rows.claim: Ali, Hatib ibn Abi Baltaʿa, Hasan, and Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ read المصور with fatḥa on the wāw and in the accusative, as an object of al-Bāriʾ, meaning the genus of image-makers.
rows.anchor: ابن السمقيع ( المصور ) بفتح الواو والنصب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali also read المصور with fatḥa on the wāw and kasra on the rāʾ, as a construct phrase with the object, like the one striking the boy.
rows.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه فتح الواو وكسر الراء

rows.speaker: الخانية
rows.claim: Al-Khāniyya says that reading المصور with fatḥa on the wāw invalidates prayer; al-Alusi allows this if it is construed as an attribute of God and otherwise questions the ruling.
rows.anchor: بفتح الواو هنا تفسد الصلاة ولعله أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most beautiful names denote the finest meanings.
rows.anchor: له الأسماء الحسنى ( الدالة على محاسن المعاني

words: يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All beings glorify God by the language of their state, through the wisdoms and benefits in them, or by actual speech in a manner suited to each, as many mystics hold.
rows.anchor: من الموجودات بلسان الحال لما تضمنته من الحكم والمصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two names gather all perfections: al-Aziz signals perfect power as the overpowering, and al-Hakim signals perfect knowledge through action according to wisdom.
rows.anchor: الجامع للكمالات كافة فإنها مع تكثرها وتشعبها راجعة إلى كمال القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending suggests adorning with divine perfections after declaring God incomparable, as in 42:11.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى التحلية بعد التخلية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن معقل بن يسار
rows.claim: Whoever says the seeking-refuge formula three times morning or evening and reads the last three verses of al-Hashr has 70,000 angels pray for him until the opposite time; if he dies that day or night, he dies a martyr. Al-Tirmidhi graded the report hasan.
rows.anchor: عن معقل بن يسار عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says that God’s greatest name occurs in the six final verses of al-Hashr.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس مرفوعا اسم الله الأعظم في ست آيات

rows.speaker: علي عن البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara asked Ali for the prayer taught to him by the Prophet through Gabriel; Ali prescribed the first ten verses of al-Hadid, the end of al-Hashr, and an invocation beginning ‘O One who is thus.’
rows.anchor: قال لعليابن أبي طالب كرم الله تعالى وجهه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن علي وابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the verse beginning ‘If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain’ is a remedy for headache.
rows.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه مرفوعا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A report traced through reciters from Khalaf back to the Prophet says to place a hand on the head while reciting the mountain verse; Gabriel said it heals every illness except death.
rows.anchor: بد الله رضي الله تعالى عنه فلما بلغنا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is commonly named al-Mumtaḥana with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, though kasra is also used: the former describes the woman connected with its revelation, the latter the sūra, like al-Barāʾa’s epithet al-Fāḍiḥa.
rows.anchor: المشهور في هذه التسمية أنها بفتح الحاء وقد تكسر

rows.speaker: جمال القراء
rows.claim: Jamāl al-Qurrāʾ also records the names al-Imtiḥān and Sūrat al-Mawadda.
rows.anchor: تسمى أيضا الامتحان وسورة المودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr state that the sūra is Medinan; others say its opening was revealed at the conquest of Mecca, with the Medinan label reflecting either the predominant portion or the definition revealed after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وهي ثلاث عشرة آية بالاتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra contains thirteen verses by consensus.
rows.anchor: وهي ثلاث عشرة آية بالاتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hashr describes hypocrites’ alliance with disbelieving People of the Book; al-Mumtaḥana forbids believers to ally with disbelievers so they do not resemble hypocrites, and develops that prohibition at length.
rows.anchor: أنه ذكر فيها قبل موالاة الذين نافقوا للذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another connection says the previous sūra mentions treaty People of the Book, while this one mentions treaty polytheists and includes material revealed at Hudaybiyya; this explains its placement before al-Saff despite their shared tasbīḥ opening.
rows.anchor: إن فيما قبل ذكر المعاهدين من أهل الكتاب وفي هذه ذكر المعاهدين من المشركين
